issues.legal_issue: A finding that a land transfer was made to cause loss to the State cannot be sustained when a principal basis for the finding is that the rent was unusually low, but there is no evidence of the prevailing rent for comparable land at the relevant time.
material_facts: The revenue authorities annulled a settlement made in 1946, reasoning in part that its rent of Rs. 3 per katha was very low and that the settlement was intended to cause loss to the State.
The authorities and the High Court relied on the alleged low rent as a principal consideration, but no evidence established the prevailing rental rate for similar land when the settlement was made.
The appellant challenged the annulment orders in a constitutional petition, which the High Court dismissed; the appellant appealed by certificate.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed and the impugned orders were set aside because a principal consideration underlying them was based on assumptions and conjecture, not evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(b) of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950 empowers the Collector, after reasonable notice, to annul a transfer made after 1 January 1946 if satisfied that it was made to defeat the Act, cause loss to the State, or obtain higher compensation. A finding supporting annulment must have an evidentiary basis; treating rent as very low without evidence of the rate prevailing for comparable land at the relevant time is insufficient. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.transfer_annulment_proceeding: Land-revenue authorities conducted a proceeding to annul a transfer made after an estate vested in the State.
predicates.officials_relied_on_low_rent_as_a_princi: The authorities treated the rent agreed for the transfer as unusually low and relied on that assessment as a principal basis for finding that the transfer was intended to cause loss to the State.
predicates.evidence_of_comparable_rent: Evidence established the prevailing rental rate at the relevant time for land comparable to the transferred land.
predicates.annulment_order_invalid: The order annulling the transfer cannot stand.

issues.definition: If authorities seek to annul a transfer and principally rely on the rent being unusually low without evidence of the prevailing rent for comparable land, the annulment order cannot stand.
